events.text: At the old shoreline stands a cairn of salt blocks, and in its hollow someone left two sealed jerrycans for the next traveller. A note in the lid says: 'Ring for us when you can.'
The glare off the pan is blinding at the Cut. Then the glare grows engines.
Wind moans through the rusted lifeboat half sunk in the salt. Every few breaths a loose plate swings and strikes the hull - a deep, drowning note that rolls across the basin.
A mirror flashes three times from the top of the basalt: the scouts of Basalt Watch have seen you, and they are letting you know.
A salt storm scours the paint off your doors - and uncovers a buried cache of fuel drums by the road.
The crust gives way under a wheel. By the time you have winched the truck out of the brine, a tire is shredded.
On the horizon a long water caravan shimmers in the heat. Then it bends, doubles, and is gone. The Bell Folk say the salt shows you what you want most.
A hermit in a coat of sewn sacks trades you screws from a dead ship for a single cup of water, then walks back into the white without a word.
Beside the track stands a little wooden shrine with a little bell - and under it, three sealed skins of water. The pilgrims remembered you.
